questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not lower your BAC or reduce alcohol's effects. They may help you stay alert, but they cannot make you sober.

questions.question: Driving has risks. It is smart to keep improving your driving and observation skills.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Driving is unsafe if drivers think they have nothing to learn. Always work to improve your driving and observation skills to protect yourself and others.

questions.question: You are angry after something that happened at work. When you reach your car, you should:

options.text: Play loud music so you do not think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to release stress.
Calm down for a few minutes before driving home.
Stop at a bar for drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down for a few minutes before driving home.
questions.explanation: If you feel upset or angry, take time to calm down before you drive. Driving while emotional is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely:

options.text: A deaf person.
Conducting a traffic study.
A blind person.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A blind person.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians with white canes or guide dogs cross first. They have the right-of-way.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, the effects of alcohol go away only by:

options.text: Taking a cold shower.
Waiting several hours.
Drinking several cups of coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Waiting several hours.
questions.explanation: Time is the only way alcohol leaves your body. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: You should not stop suddenly in front of large trucks and buses because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses well in their mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.
Large trucks and buses drive faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles take longer to stop than small vehicles. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle may cause a crash because the driver cannot stop in time.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to all emergency vehicles using lights, sirens, or horns. Pull to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: When a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane crosses the street:

options.text: You must always let them cross first.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only have to let them cross at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always let them cross first.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind people use white canes or guide dogs. You must always give them the right-of-way when they are crossing.

questions.question: You can spot an aggressive driver by:

options.text: Sudden and improper lane changes.
How many passengers are in their car.
Their habit of driving slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sudden and improper lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch for aggressive drivers who make sudden or improper lane changes. Do not challenge them. The safest thing is to let them pass.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Must stop for them.
Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must stop for pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing illegally in the middle of the street.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt?

options.text: The driver
Front seat passengers
Children under age 13
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Oklahoma law requires all front seat occupants to wear a seat belt. Children under 13 must wear a seat belt in any seat.

questions.question: How should you safely cross railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are dangerous. Always look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings are warning signs. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns of low clearance ahead.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic is blocking an intersection?

options.text: Use your horn to get traffic to move.
Drive closely to the car ahead in case the light turns red.
Wait to enter the intersection until you can cross it completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait to enter the intersection until you can cross it completely.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way through. Wait until traffic ahead clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when a police officer stops you?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel during a traffic stop. Tell passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Get some coffee.
Open your window.
Stop driving.
Turn on the radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop driving.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: What do temporary signs in construction zones look like?

options.text: Red background with green writing.
Orange background with black writing.
Yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Visibility is lower at night. Take these steps to stay safe and protect other drivers.

questions.question: What is a distraction when driving?

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. They can cause crashes, injuries, and death.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:

options.text: Have the right-of-way.
Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: If you are entering traffic from a driveway or private road, yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is possible.
